title.narrative: Emergency Responses to conflict affected internally displaced persons (IDPs) in Magwi County

description.narrative: This project is initiated to respond to the needs of IDPs displaced by farmers/herders conflict in Magwi County Eastern Equatoria State. On 18th January 2025, herders from Jonglei State relocated to Ayii and Nyolo in Magwi County, leading to extensive crop destruction and displacement of the host community. The estimated number of cattle brought into Ayii and Nyolo ranges between 8,000 and 10,000, resulting in the destruction of nearly 100 hectares of farmland. The herders' pledge to compensate was rejected by the host community, who demanded their immediate departure. Negotiation efforts failed, and on 31st January 2025, conflict erupted between the two communities. Eye Radio reports indicate that 41 people were killed in the raids, though this figure remains unverified. Confirmed casualties include 29 host community members dead, three missing, and nearly 22,000 internally displaced, bringing the total fatalities to 70. Additionally, reports confirm widespread burning and looting of houses and properties, including livestock, with an estimated 7,000–9,000 heads of cattle raided. On 1st February 2025, reports emerged of destruction and looting in Agoro Centre, including the vandalization of youth and women's centres supported by UNHCR. In response, the host community mainly women and children fled toward Magwi Centre,Obama, obo, Pajok and Iwonkibook.
